topic: Global sound-and-complete macro-effect identification under arbitrary variable clustering. Input a finite feasible arbitrary cluster causal diagram H with known cluster memberships and finite micro alphabets, together with disjoint macro intervention and outcome sets. Over all recursive semi-Markovian finite SCMs whose acyclic micro ADMG coarsens exactly to H and whose observational law is strictly positive, construct Global-CID: a terminating graph-native algorithm that returns either one guarded arithmetic circuit F(P(V)) for the full P(C_Y | do(C_X=c_x)), valid simultaneously for every compatible law, SCM, and intervention value, or a bounded-cardinality collision certificate containing compatible micro refinements and two strictly positive finite SCMs with the same complete observed law but different target distributions. Prove soundness, completeness, termination, and an explicit elementary complexity/output bound in the finite encoded input. The decisive kernel is a constructive overlap normal-form theorem that either compiles refinement-specific identifying formulas into one circuit on all common-law overlaps or extracts an actual common-law separating pair; generic real quantifier elimination may verify a returned certificate but is not the identification algorithm. After a formula return, derive empirical-multinomial plug-in influence inference on fixed positive-support strata and simultaneous-region propagation across guarded boundaries. Treat Anand-Hripcsak's ALARM medical C-DAG effect analysis and the cyclic lisinopril-stroke grouping as consumers.

open_problems.open_problem: Can refinement-specific causal-effect formulas be normalized constructively so that they compile into one guarded circuit exactly when they agree on every common strictly positive observable-law overlap?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a sufficient common-formula criterion across candidate Markov-equivalence classes, not a complete overlap-sensitive criterion.
source_refs.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, Terry Soo

source_refs.claim: For small finite functional causal structures, algebraic elimination can characterize observable equivalence and identifiable parameters.
source_refs.author: Ciarán M. Lee, Robert W. Spekkens

source_refs.excerpt: The boundary-face correction must survive nonlinear district gluing before global completeness can be claimed.
A finite canonical parameterization makes global identification decidable by real algebraic methods

open_problems.why_unsolved: Robust-ID and PAG completeness operate on constrained graph-uncertainty representations, while algebraic methods can compare tiny finite models only through generic elimination. None decides the semantic case where different formulas are correct on their own model images and must be compared only on the intersection of those images. The prior district-transport run identifies the same local-to-global failure: a one-district active face can outer-relax the true nonlinear multi-district compatibility projection. The missing first step is a finite normalization of fixing-derived rational formulas modulo each overlap's graph-implied equalities and positivity guards, with either a proof of equality on the overlap or an executable separating law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite overlap-normal-form theorem that rewrites all locally valid formulas into a common guarded arithmetic circuit exactly when they coincide on every nonempty positive-law overlap, and otherwise extracts an overlap law with two different target values.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly frames causal identification that must remain valid across several non-equivalent structural candidates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal effects depend on structural assumptions -> discovery can leave non-equivalent candidate graphs -> conclusions should be robust across candidates -> completeness requires overlap-sensitive rather than free-simplex formula agreement

method_exemplars.technique: Compare causal-effect expressions across candidate MPDAGs and certify a shared evaluation under graphical invariance conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest direct treatment of one effect functional across multiple non-Markov-equivalent candidates; the new theorem must make the criterion necessary and overlap-aware.

method_exemplars.technique: Polynomially parameterize finite functional causal models and eliminate latent parameters to expose semialgebraic observable-model constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The overlap is an intersection of finite semialgebraic observable models, so this supplies a semantic oracle against which the required graph-symbolic normal form can be proved complete.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive influence functions from fixing-based identifying functionals and project them using observed-law equality constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A compiled overlap-normal formula is still a fixing-derived observed-law functional, and its guards determine which branchwise influence curves represent the same target.

open_problems.open_problem: Does a terminating sound-and-complete graph-native procedure exist for macro-effect identification over every acyclic micro-ADMG that coarsens to an arbitrary feasible cluster graph, including cyclic directed cluster quotients?

source_refs.claim: C-DAG identification is sound and complete for acyclic cluster diagrams, while cyclic cluster partitions are excluded.
source_refs.author: Tara V. Anand, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Arbitrary clustering need not preserve effect identifiability; transit clusters give preservation only for a restricted contraction class.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Jouni Helske, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.excerpt: The load-bearing claim is district-compositional compression with a checkable signed countermodel trace.
construction and semantic completeness of that system remain entirely open

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest cluster-level completeness theorem treats the cluster graph itself as acyclic, but an arbitrary partition of an acyclic micrograph can create a cyclic quotient. Transit-cluster results cover only contractions satisfying special structural conditions. Prior CausalSmith runs also separate finite algebraic decidability from a graph-native compositional calculus: an exponential verifier or a finite response-type oracle does not provide local rules, a decreasing search invariant, or circuit-output bounds. Ordinary ID can solve each fixed refinement, but its recursion neither reconciles different refinement images nor turns global failure into a cross-refinement same-law collision.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph-native algorithm with an explicit elementary termination and output bound that returns either one guarded observational functional valid for every compatible refinement and intervention value or two bounded compatible finite SCMs with the same positive observed law and different macro effects.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest application-driven progression from incomplete micrograph knowledge to cluster-level causal queries and exposes the acyclicity boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: fully specified micrographs are unrealistic in high-dimensional domains -> cluster diagrams encode coarser causal knowledge -> existing C-DAG identification handles acyclic cluster graphs -> arbitrary feasible clustering requires a formula-or-collision result even for cyclic quotients

method_exemplars.technique: Recursive district decomposition with hedge-based completeness, including a constructive nonidentifiability argument when ID fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each compatible micro-ADMG is an ordinary recursive semi-Markovian instance, so this is the local complete engine that the global procedure must lift.

method_exemplars.technique: Use invariant graphical structure to identify an effect throughout a graph equivalence class and characterize failure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both tasks require a causal answer robust to graph uncertainty, but cluster refinements span different observable model sets rather than one PAG equivalence class.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile fixing-based identification formulas into weighting and influence-function estimators with graphical tangent-space arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful global circuit is assembled from the same fixing, marginalization, and conditionalization operations and therefore has a concrete estimation-and-inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Can every failure of uniform macro-effect identification be converted constructively into two bounded finite recursive semi-Markovian SCMs with the same strictly positive complete observed law, exact active micrographs coarsening to the declared cluster graph, and different targets?

source_refs.claim: For one known semi-Markovian graph, ID failure is characterized by a hedge and entails observationally indistinguishable models with different intervention distributions.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: Discrete-observed SCM counterfactual laws admit a finite canonical exogenous representation for a fixed causal diagram.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: current construction jointly preserves positivity, normalized selected-law equality, rationality, and outcome contrast.
The source-product and shared-mechanism lift is therefore not asserted by the certificate

open_problems.why_unsolved: A hedge supplies a separator for one fixed graph, and canonical-response reductions make one discrete causal model finite, but neither result simultaneously enforces strict observed positivity, activity of every advertised micro edge, equality of the entire observed law across two possibly different refinements, and a macro-target contrast. The prior S-ID and disturbance-probe runs expose the same legality gap: an algebraic null direction or projected kernel contrast need not lift to independent latent roots and shared observed mechanisms. The first source construction that must change is the ordinary binary hedge pair, which must be positivity-smoothed and exactified in two refinement-specific SCMs without adding forbidden macro adjacencies or erasing the target contrast.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating separator-lift theorem with an explicit elementary latent-support bound and a finite checker for exact coarsening, graph activity, observed-law equality, positivity, and target separation.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes completeness as a duality between an identifying expression and an actual indistinguishable-model obstruction, which is the right certificate narrative.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: a causal query may not be determined by observations -> graphical failure should yield genuinely indistinguishable causal models -> hedges provide that witness for one graph -> cluster uncertainty requires a bounded positive witness spanning refinements

method_exemplars.technique: Construct observationally equivalent causal models from nested C-forests while forcing the intervention distributions to differ.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the canonical constructive nonidentification proof that must be strengthened to positivity, exact graph activity, and cross-refinement collisions.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace arbitrary exogenous variables by finite response-function types while preserving factual and counterfactual distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A bounded collision certificate needs this finite canonicalization, followed by a new paired exactification step that retains active edges.

open_problems.open_problem: For a guarded family of rational macro-effect formulas over a union of refinement models, when is the empirical-multinomial plug-in regular, and how can simultaneous coverage remain valid near guard and overlap boundaries?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives influence-function estimators for a broad hidden-variable class while leaving general identifiable effects and richer treatment structures as extensions.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: For directionally differentiable functionals the ordinary bootstrap generally fails, but derivative-aware resampling can recover local validity.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: Extend the inference layer to branch ties through a directional delta method and resampling procedure
The scope excludes inference at branch boundaries

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing graphical semiparametric theory differentiates one fixed identifying functional. A Global-CID output can instead switch algebraic branch when compatibility or equality guards change, so empirical branch selection may have different linearizations even when population formulas agree. The prior reviewer explicitly identifies branch ties as an unclosed inference layer. The first proof step that fails is the ordinary smooth delta method: it must be replaced by a stratified or Hadamard-directional derivative of the whole guarded selection map, including a data-dependent near-active guard set and local sequences that cross refinement boundaries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving branchwise influence functions and joint Gaussian limits on regular positive-support strata, plus either a uniformly valid derivative-aware resampling or simultaneous-region procedure at guard intersections or an explicit local-nonregularity impossibility result.

writing_exemplar.why: It moves directly from graphical identification to estimators and uncertainty quantification, allowing guarded refinement boundaries to be isolated as the new statistical layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: graphical identification yields observed-law functionals -> empirical use requires influence analysis -> fixed-graph theory covers smooth functionals -> guarded multi-refinement formulas require boundary-robust inference

method_exemplars.technique: Derive branchwise influence functions from fixing and nested-factorization formulas and project onto graph-restricted tangent spaces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every smooth guard branch is an identified hidden-variable graphical functional of this type.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the Hadamard directional delta method and estimate the directional derivative through a modified bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Guard switching creates a finite piecewise-smooth map whose boundary behavior is directional rather than ordinarily differentiable.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert tests over graph structures and numerical parameters instead of conditioning on a selected graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A simultaneous region must retain refinement uncertainty rather than report an interval conditional on one empirically selected branch.

open_problems.open_problem: When a macro effect is not uniformly point identified over compatible micro-refinements, what are its sharp law-specific bounds over the refinement union?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives analytical causal-effect bounds when structural uncertainty is represented by a PAG.
source_refs.author: Alexis Bellot

source_refs.claim: For a specified discrete causal graph, causal bounding reduces to polynomial programming with certified epsilon-sharp computation and inference.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: PAG bounds exploit invariants of one Markov-equivalence class, while autobounds encodes one specified canonical causal graph. An arbitrary cluster graph denotes a finite union of non-equivalent micro-ADMG models and may have a cyclic quotient; sharpness at a fixed observed law requires every refinement-specific program to share exactly the same observed probability coordinates. The donor method is finite response-function polynomial optimization, but its single-graph canonical reduction must be replaced by a disjunctive refinement-indexed program with common-law constraints and a proof that the envelope over refinements is attainable. The focused scan found fixed-graph and PAG bounds, not this arbitrary-cluster union problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite polynomial or mixed-disjunctive characterization whose extrema equal the sharp macro-effect identified set across all compatible refinements at a fixed positive observed law, with certified epsilon-sharp computation and an asymptotically valid confidence region for its endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames partial identification as the principled response when causal-structure uncertainty prevents a unique effect.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: a unique causal graph is rarely credible -> structural uncertainty can destroy point identification -> bounds retain every compatible effect -> arbitrary clusters require sharp bounds over a larger refinement union

method_exemplars.technique: Translate discrete SCM response types, observed evidence, and causal targets into a polynomial program and prove that its global extrema are sharp bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each compatible refinement contributes exactly such a finite program; the new mathematical object is their common-observed-law union.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize arbitrary discrete SCMs to finite exogenous domains before optimizing counterfactual targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its finite canonical-family theorem is the natural basis for proving that the refinement-union bounds omit no compatible SCM.

method_exemplars.technique: Use calibrated bootstrap projection over relaxed sample moment inequalities to obtain confidence intervals with uniform asymptotic coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired endpoints are extrema of a constrained finite-dimensional identified set and need coverage that survives changing active refinements.

open_problems.open_problem: Can complete generalized identification from arbitrary surrogate experiments be lifted from one known causal graph to an arbitrary-cluster refinement class with overlap agreement and cross-refinement collision certificates?

source_refs.claim: gID is sound and complete for identifying an effect from arbitrary surrogate experiments under one specified causal diagram.
source_refs.author: Sanghack Lee, Juan D. Correa, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: CTFID is complete for nested counterfactual identification from arbitrary observational and experimental distributions under a specified graph.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Sanghack Lee, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The C-DAG framework lifts causal identification to clusters but formally excludes cyclic cluster diagrams.
source_refs.author: Tara V. Anand, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: gID and CTFID prove completeness by decomposing kernels in one fixed graph, while existing C-DAG lifting treats an acyclic macrograph as a causal model. The destination has neither a unique micrograph nor necessarily an acyclic quotient. The donor method is hedgelet/thicket-based generalized ID; its first proof step that changes is the fixed-graph district decomposition, which must run refinement-wise and then reconcile answers on shared observational-and-experimental-law overlaps. The focused search found complete generalized ID, nested counterfactual ID, and acyclic C-DAGs, but no complete data-fusion algorithm over arbitrary clustered refinements.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating sound-and-complete cluster-global gID algorithm returning a guarded functional of the available observational and surrogate-experimental laws exactly when all compatible refinements agree, and otherwise bounded finite SCMs sharing every supplied law but disagreeing on the target.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames generalized identification as fusion of heterogeneous experimental inputs and organizes the result around completeness, formula output, and graphical failure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: observational data may not identify an effect -> surrogate experiments can supply missing causal information -> gID completely fuses experiments for one graph -> cluster uncertainty requires the guarantee uniformly across refinements

method_exemplars.technique: Use generalized district recursion with hedgelets and thickets to prove both formula soundness and non-gID completeness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the complete fixed-graph engine whose outputs must be reconciled across the refinement family.

method_exemplars.technique: Unnest counterfactuals and factor them into counterfactual components before reduction to supplied experimental laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how complete identification survives richer targets and heterogeneous inputs, providing the closest template for a clustered data-fusion extension.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert nested-factorization identifying functionals into influence-function and weighting estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful clustered gID formula is a finite composition of kernels from observed or experimental distributions and therefore admits this estimation rung.

literature_map:
Anand, Ribeiro, Tian, and Bareinboim (AAAI 2023; arXiv:2202.12263) prove sound and complete identification for acyclic C-DAGs but exclude cyclic cluster quotients.
Tikka, Helske, and Karvanen (JMLR 2023; arXiv:2111.04513) show arbitrary clustering can change identifiability and isolate the safer transit-cluster regime.
Shpitser and Pearl (AAAI 2006) give complete ID for one recursive semi-Markovian graph, pairing formulas with hedge-based witnesses.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (2017; arXiv:1701.06686) recast hidden-variable identification through nested-Markov fixing and kernels.
Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (ICML 2019; arXiv:1812.06209) give complete effect identification for graph uncertainty represented by one PAG.
Perković (UAI 2020) supplies a necessary-and-sufficient effect criterion for MPDAGs without latent variables.
Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (ICML 2025; arXiv:2506.15561) span several candidate classes but give a sufficient rather than complete robust-ID criterion.
Lee and Spekkens (JCI 2017; arXiv:1506.03880) use computational algebraic geometry for finite observational equivalence and identifiable parameters.
Evans (Scandinavian Journal of Statistics 2016; arXiv:1408.1809) shows ordinary mixed graphs do not capture every marginal-model distinction.
Wolfe, Spekkens, and Fritz (JCI 2019; arXiv:1609.00672) and Navascués and Wolfe (JCI 2020; arXiv:1707.06476) develop causal-compatibility inflation hierarchies.
Duarte et al. (JASA 2024; arXiv:2109.13471) reduce fixed-graph discrete causal bounds to certified polynomial programs.
Bellot (UAI 2024) derives effect bounds under PAG uncertainty, not arbitrary cluster-refinement unions.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2022; arXiv:2110.05690) give finite canonical-SCM reductions for fixed-graph counterfactual problems.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022; arXiv:2003.12659) develop fixing-based influence-function estimators while leaving broader identifiable effects open.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (UAI 2020) and Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2021) give complete generalized and nested-counterfactual ID under one graph; no arbitrary-cluster analogue was found.
